observations.observation_value: Five complete chronic traumatic SCI patients underwent SSEP/MEP-guided scar excision, autologous BMMC-loaded NeuroRegen scaffold implantation, and 12-month follow-up.
observations.normalized_value: chronic complete human scaffold implantation feasible in small cohort
observations.statistics_reported: small cohort; adverse-event detail requires full source review
observations.notes: Feasibility signal only; not efficacy proof.

observations.observation_value: Eight chronic complete ASIA A SCI patients received 4 x 10^7 hUCB-MSCs on NeuroRegen after SSEP/MEP-guided scar resection. No treatment-related adverse events occurred over 1 year; sensation expanded in 5/8 and MEP-responsive area in 7/8, while ASIA grade did not improve.
observations.normalized_value: chronic complete human NeuroRegen/hUCB-MSC feasibility cohort with partial neurological signals
observations.statistics_reported: 5/8 sensation expansion; 7/8 MEP-area expansion; no ASIA grade improvement
observations.notes: Similar intervention family as M2A-P001 but different cell source; rehabilitation and uncontrolled baseline limit efficacy inference.

observations.observation_value: Porous PLGA/poly-l-lysine scaffolds implanted after thoracic lateral hemisection improved locomotor recovery in fully hemisected monkeys compared with non-implanted controls and showed appositional healing/tissue remodeling at 12 weeks.
observations.normalized_value: primate scaffold implantation improved locomotion and remodeling
observations.statistics_reported: significant improvement reported in abstract
observations.notes: Strong translational bridge but still abstract-level here.

observations.observation_value: A 2-mm PEGDA-GelMA scaffold with 200-micrometer channels retained its structure for 4 weeks, reduced reactive-cell layer thickness by 35% versus agarose, reduced GFAP scarring, vascularized, and supported 97 +/- 8 NF200-positive axons per channel; empty scaffolds did not produce distal host-axon extension.
observations.normalized_value: 3D architecture supports integration and host axon entry, but not complete relay by itself
observations.statistics_reported: P < 0.0019 for reactive layer; P < 0.0001 for GFAP; n = 11-12
observations.notes: Empty-scaffold result is separated from NPC-dependent functional relay.

observations.observation_value: In adult female C57BL/6J T9-10 lateral hemisection, porous PEG tubes showed transient dendritic-cell/macrophage enrichment at 1 week that resolved by 2 weeks and reduced glial scar thickness to 127 +/- 73 micrometers versus 337 +/- 169 micrometers with gelfoam.
observations.normalized_value: modular PEG tubes integrate without prolonged inflammatory amplification and reduce peripheral scar thickness
observations.statistics_reported: n = 3-5/timepoint; tube scar reduction reported in Fig. 4
observations.notes: Immune resolution and scar outcomes are distinct from later axon density.

observations.observation_value: PLGA 85:15 scaffolds were fabricated with parallel channels to enable testing of scaffold architecture, transplanted cells, and local molecular agents for axon regeneration.
observations.normalized_value: multi-channel PLGA scaffold as combinatorial repair platform
observations.statistics_reported: not applicable
observations.notes: Primarily platform/architecture evidence, not direct functional outcome.

observations.observation_value: Self-assembling peptide nanofiber scaffold with neural progenitor and Schwann cells supported host-cell migration, blood-vessel growth, and axonal ingrowth into rat dorsal-column transection sites.
observations.normalized_value: SAPNS creates permissive 3D ingrowth environment
observations.statistics_reported: exact values not extracted
observations.notes: Early peptide scaffold bridge anchor.

observations.observation_value: In T9 complete transection rats, aligned CNT/GelMA fibers plus ES reduced Iba1/CS56, increased NF/beta-tubulin III fibers and remyelination across the lesion, restored tissue conductivity to 1.50 x 10^-3 S/cm versus normal 2.13 x 10^-3, and produced the strongest BBB, pain, and MEP recovery.
observations.normalized_value: conductive aligned scaffold plus ES promotes neural alignment, conduction, and repair
observations.statistics_reported: Exact conductivity and 8-week endpoint direction extracted; MEP n=3/group
observations.notes: CNTs remained at the lesion; scaffold and ES effects are bundled.

observations.observation_value: hMSC-seeded PLGA scaffolds implanted into 2-mm complete rat spinal cord defects improved BBB scores and MEP amplitudes relative to scaffold-only controls.
observations.normalized_value: PLGA+hMSC improved function/electrophysiology vs scaffold-only
observations.statistics_reported: abstract reports approximate BBB 5 vs 2 and MEP 200-300 uV
observations.notes: Useful because scaffold-only comparator is present.

observations.observation_value: In adult female Fischer rat thoracic contusion, iPN supported approximately 3-fold more transplanted SCs at 14 days and twice as many SC-myelinated axons at 8 weeks versus Matrigel, with comparable BBB performance; grid-walk errors favored iPN at 4 weeks but equalized by 8 weeks.
observations.normalized_value: iPN improves graft survival and axon histology versus Matrigel without durable locomotor superiority
observations.unit: relative cell/axon count; BBB; grid-walk error
observations.statistics_reported: iPN graft volume 0.95 +/- 0.28 vs 0.48 +/- 0.17 mm3; SC-myelinated axons 6927 +/- 2429 vs 3259 +/- 475
observations.notes: iPN immune-cell numbers resembled injury-only controls at 14 days; matrix was not visible at 8 weeks, consistent with degradation.

observations.observation_value: In adult rat T10 complete transection, an NT-3-Schwann-cell/TrkC-NSC gelatin scaffold supported graft survival and MBP-positive myelin around GFP-positive graft-derived and host NF+ axons at 8 weeks; in vitro APC+ oligodendrocytic differentiation reached 12.98 +/- 5.33% in the dual-engineered group.
observations.normalized_value: engineered cell/scaffold network promotes myelination
observations.statistics_reported: MBP histology and APC value extracted; functional recovery was not the primary endpoint
observations.notes: Scaffold, engineered cells, NT-3, TrkC, and immunosuppression are bundled.

observations.observation_value: In adult female Long Evans rats with complete 2-mm T9 ablation, fibrin with a heparin-binding delivery system and NT-3 (1000 ng/mL) increased overall Tuj1 fiber density to 10.4% versus 3% saline and approximately 6-7% fibrin controls, while fibrin reduced white-matter-border GFAP.
observations.normalized_value: NT-3 fibrin scaffold improved early histology without later functional improvement
observations.statistics_reported: F-DS-NT3 1000 ng/mL; 9-day endpoint
observations.notes: Key positive-histology/negative-function boundary; no neuronal cell bodies were observed in the lesion.

observations.observation_value: Structured HA hydrogel with anti-NgR and BDNF/VEGF-loaded PLGA microspheres integrated with host tissue, inhibited inflammation/gliosis, increased vessels and regenerated fibers, and improved locomotor recovery after rat dorsal hemisection.
observations.normalized_value: HA+PLGA multi-cargo scaffold improved repair profile
observations.statistics_reported: exact values not extracted
observations.notes: Multiple active components make attribution difficult.

observations.observation_value: Eight-percent SilMA with PLGA microspheres released >40% of Ang-(1-7) within 3 days and nearly all by 7 days, while NT-3 release persisted through days 28-56 in PBS release testing.
observations.normalized_value: staged release scaffold targets early inflammation then later neuroregeneration
observations.statistics_reported: Ang-(1-7) >40% by day 3 and nearly complete by day 7; NT-3 remained in delayed release through days 28-56
observations.notes: In-vitro PBS release does not establish the same in-vivo kinetics.

observations.outcome_type: Integration, angiogenesis, axon ingrowth, and host response
observations.observation_value: In male Wistar Th8 hemisection, 8 mg/mL porcine spinal-cord or urinary-bladder ECM hydrogels integrated into the lesion, increased NF160 axon ingrowth and RECA vascularization versus saline, and modulated early inflammatory gene expression, but massive macrophage infiltration, rapid degradation, and progressive small cysts limited reconstruction.
observations.normalized_value: injectable ECM supports tissue bridging and ingrowth but rapid degradation and macrophage response limit durable repair
observations.statistics_reported: n = 5/group/timepoint; qPCR at 2, 4, 8 weeks
observations.notes: SC-ECM and UB-ECM were not significantly different; functional recovery was not established.

observations.observation_value: In adult rat T8 dorsal hemisection, protoplasmic astrocyte ECM in HA reduced GFAP area around the lesion (9.7 +/- 1.1% vs sham 16 +/- 3.3%), ED1 area around the lesion (5.5 +/- 0.97% vs sham 9.7 +/- 1.6%), and increased Tuj1 area in the lesion (14 +/- 1.0% vs sham 9.2 +/- 1.9%); fibrous ECM did not reproduce the benefit.
observations.normalized_value: astrocyte ECM subtype changes HA hydrogel histology and immune response
observations.statistics_reported: Exact values extracted; 2 weeks after implantation, 4 weeks after injury
observations.notes: No functional locomotor test; ECM source and cell-loading effects remain separate boundaries.

observations.evidence_type: Chronic scar removal plus anisotropic hydrogel
observations.observation_value: Anisotropic alginate hydrogels implanted after scar removal at 4 WPI in chronic complete thoracic transection supported electrophysiological conductivity, locomotor improvement, host-cell migration, reduced scarring, and multiple tract classes growing through/beyond channels.
observations.normalized_value: chronic scar-removal alginate scaffold supports structural and functional repair
observations.statistics_reported: outcomes up to 3 months; exact stats not extracted
observations.notes: Strong chronic bridge to Module 1, but abstract-level here.

observations.evidence_type: Chronic canine scar removal plus NeuroRegen/hUC-MSC
observations.observation_value: In 18 adult female beagles with complete T8 resection, delayed scar removal and functionalized NeuroRegen implantation (n=6) produced Olby scores of approximately 6 versus 2-4.5 in control or scaffold-only groups by 12 months, with reduced CS-56/CSPG signal in both scaffold groups.
observations.normalized_value: large-animal chronic NeuroRegen+hUC-MSC repair signal with scaffold and cell contributions separated
observations.statistics_reported: Functionalized scaffold reached approximately Olby 6; scaffold-only groups plateaued at 2-4.5; n=6/group
observations.notes: Scar removal did not worsen locomotion; functional benefit is confounded by surgery, scaffold, cells, and rehabilitation.

observations.observation_value: In female SD rats with 200 kdyn T8 contusion, one-week post-injury surface capping with HA/PPY/PM-CURC-iNPC preserved beta-III-tubulin fibers, reduced GFAP-negative lesion area and PDGF expression, and did not worsen gross tissue structure; iNPCs mainly showed astroglial rather than neuronal colocalization and Iba1/ED1 inflammation did not differ at one week.
observations.normalized_value: surface-capping conductive scaffold supports cells and early repair-associated responses
observations.statistics_reported: n=3/group; one-week post-implant endpoint
observations.notes: Early small-N study; no long-term function and no early anti-inflammatory benefit.

observations.observation_value: Schwann-cell exosome and methylprednisolone composite patch improved rat SCI functional and electrophysiological performance, shifted macrophages toward M2-type response, reduced inflammatory response, and increased neuronal survival.
observations.normalized_value: exosome/steroid surface patch modulates inflammation and repair
observations.statistics_reported: exact values not extracted
observations.notes: Patch covers hematoma surface rather than filling cavity.

observations.observation_value: In acute unilateral cervical resection rats, NF+ axons followed OEC/host-cell trajectories but increased only as a trend over non-seeded or untreated lesions; both seeded and non-seeded microstructured collagen scaffolds improved skilled forelimb function, and function was not correlated with scaffold axon extent.
observations.normalized_value: functional recovery can dissociate from scaffold-traversing axon regeneration
observations.statistics_reported: Exact mechanistic direction extracted; source does not establish a simple bridge-mediated recovery mechanism
observations.notes: Strong negative-mechanism boundary; no single biomaterial/cell component explains recovery.

observations.observation_value: Two acute complete patients (T11 treated at approximately 24 hours; C4 at 8 days) received approximately 4 x 10^7 umbilical-cord MSCs on 1.5-cm or 1.1-cm NeuroRegen implants. Both improved from ASIA A to C with sensory/motor gains and recovered SSEP/MEP; the thoracic patient's WISCI rose from 0 to 7 at 12 months.
observations.normalized_value: acute complete human scaffold/MSC feasibility signal
observations.statistics_reported: n=2; uncontrolled; no obvious treatment-related adverse symptoms
observations.notes: Supports feasibility and hypothesis generation only; not efficacy-grade evidence.

observations.observation_value: In rat and canine complete transection models, hUC-MSC-loaded collagen scaffolds improved locomotor and electrophysiological outcomes over SCI or scaffold-only groups: rat BBB improved at 4-8 weeks, while canine Olby scores and MEP improved more with cells at 3-6 months.
observations.normalized_value: collagen+hUC-MSC preclinical scaffold/cell strategy shows species-spanning functional and conduction signals
observations.statistics_reported: Rat n=10/group; canine n=5/group
observations.notes: Animal findings support translation but do not isolate scaffold, cell, and rehabilitation effects completely.

observations.observation_value: In adult rat C5 hemi-incision, a 1-mm PCLEEP-collagen scaffold aligned to the cord supported axon ingrowth by 1 week, sustained alignment through 4 weeks, and MAG-positive axon-associated structures at 4 weeks. NT-3 loading was 54.6 ng/mg with 90.1% released in week 1 and 99.7% by 3 months; scaffold degradation was 24.8%, 33.4%, and 51.6% at 1, 2, and 3 months in vitro.
observations.normalized_value: aligned nanofibers combine contact guidance with prolonged local trophic delivery
observations.statistics_reported: release and degradation values reported in Results
observations.notes: Functional recovery was not tested in this paper; later work is needed for neuronal reconnection.

observations.statistics_reported: exact values not extracted

observations.notes: bFGF and material effects remain partly inseparable; no clear astrocytic scar reduction versus lesion control.

observations.statistics_reported: exact values not extracted

observations.observation_value: In 14 female Beagles with right T10 4 mm hemisection, NT-3/fibroin gelatin sponge (n=7) improved 4-week Olby score to 11.85 +/- 0.64 versus 9.29 +/- 1.48 fibroin-only control, produced detectable CMEP versus negligible control signal, reduced IBA1+ cells at the graft (74.11 +/- 5.85 vs 98.41 +/- 15.43 cells/0.09 mm2), and increased NF+ fiber density; GFAP scar density was not different. EM also showed host-cell migration, vessels, synapse-like structures, and occasional MBP+ fibers in the NF-GS graft.

observations.statistics_reported: Exact Olby, IBA1, and NF/GFAP values extracted at 4 weeks
observations.notes: Large-animal, short-follow-up evidence; GFAP scar did not improve and CMEP did not prove a fully reconstructed pathway.

author_claims.claim_text: Electrophysiology-guided chronic scar resection followed by NeuroRegen scaffold plus autologous BMMC implantation is feasible in a very small complete chronic human SCI cohort.
author_claims.notes: Feasibility only; efficacy remains unproven.

author_claims.claim_text: NeuroRegen scaffold plus hUCB-MSC implantation after scar resection was safe in this small chronic complete human cohort and was associated with partial sensory/electrophysiological gains, but not ASIA grade improvement.
author_claims.notes: Uncontrolled cohort with concurrent rehabilitation; no causal efficacy claim.

author_claims.claim_text: Porous biodegradable scaffolds can promote tissue remodeling and functional improvement in non-human primate acute SCI.
author_claims.notes: Strong translational species, abstract-level extraction.

author_claims.claim_text: Aligned PEG hydrogel tubes provide modular physical guidance, transiently limit scar formation, support axon growth and partial myelination, and improve locomotion in a mouse lateral-hemisection model; tube-specific superiority over a PEG bridge was not established.
author_claims.notes: Scaffold-only gelfoam comparator and tube-versus-bridge boundary are now explicit.

author_claims.claim_text: Conductive aligned GelMA/CNT hydrogel fibers can combine regenerative scaffold guidance with electrical stimulation: in T9 transection rats the combined treatment improved inflammatory markers, axon density/remyelination, tissue conductivity, BBB, pain response, and MEP, but scaffold and stimulation contributions remain bundled.
author_claims.notes: ES protocol was 2 V for 1 h at 1, 4, and 7 days in vitro; in-vivo functional effects were measured at 8 weeks.

author_claims.claim_text: Cell-seeded PLGA scaffolds can outperform scaffold-only controls after complete transection SCI.
author_claims.notes: One of the clearer scaffold-only comparator claims.

author_claims.claim_text: Injectable decellularized peripheral nerve matrix is a clinically oriented Schwann-cell carrier that improves graft survival and myelinated-axon counts relative to Matrigel, without durable BBB superiority.
author_claims.notes: Histology benefit is stronger than locomotor superiority; iPN did not aggravate early immune infiltration.

author_claims.claim_text: Scaffold-delivered NT-3 can improve early axonal sprouting and reduce white-matter-border astroglial scar without improving motor function at 12 weeks in this ablation model.
author_claims.notes: Important histology-function dissociation; no treatment difference in macrophage/microglia density.

author_claims.claim_text: Sequential release scaffolds can align an early anti-inflammatory cue with a later neurogenic cue: Ang-(1-7) was released rapidly (>40% by day 3; nearly complete by day 7), whereas NT-3 release persisted through days 28-56, and the combined scaffold improved inflammation, neuronal markers, tissue structure, and BMS after mouse complete transection.
author_claims.source_section: Full text, release assay and Figs. 3-6
author_claims.notes: Timing is supported in vitro; combined in-vivo cargo attribution remains unresolved.

author_claims.claim_text: Injectable ECM-derived hydrogels can integrate into acute hemisection lesions and support axon and vessel ingrowth, but rapid degradation, cyst formation, macrophage infiltration, and poor cell survival constrain durable repair; spinal-cord and urinary-bladder ECM performed similarly.
author_claims.notes: Avoids treating ECM source as uniformly pro-regenerative or interchangeable with durable bridges.

author_claims.claim_text: Chronic scar removal followed by anisotropic alginate hydrogel implantation can support conduction, tract growth, and locomotor recovery in chronic complete transection SCI.
author_claims.notes: Strong chronic repair signal, but abstract-level.

author_claims.claim_text: In a controlled chronic canine transection model, scar removal plus NeuroRegen/hUC-MSC implantation improved locomotor score and lesion-site neurogenesis, remyelination, synapse signal, and secondary CSPG burden relative to controls, but the intervention is multi-component.
author_claims.notes: n=6/group; human MSC persistence was not demonstrated; rehabilitation and scar removal remain confounders.

author_claims.claim_text: Surface-applied HA demilune caps can combine conductive fibers, hydrogel cell support, and curcumin to preserve early neuronal fibers and reduce fibrotic/scar-associated signals after subacute contusion, but the one-week n=3 study did not reduce Iba1/ED1 inflammation or establish function.
author_claims.notes: Distinct intervention geometry; early endpoint and bundled components limit efficacy attribution.

author_claims.claim_text: Functional improvement after scaffold/cell treatment should not be assumed to reflect axons regenerating through the scaffold: seeded and non-seeded longitudinal collagen scaffolds both improved skilled forelimb function despite only a trend in axon counts and no correlation between function and scaffold axon extent.
author_claims.notes: Direct mechanistic boundary from the acute cervical OEC-seeded scaffold experiment.

author_claims.claim_text: Acute complete human NeuroRegen scaffold plus MSC implantation was feasible in two strictly diagnosed patients and coincided with ASIA A-to-C, sensory/motor, and SSEP/MEP recovery, but n = 2 and the uncontrolled design preclude efficacy attribution.
author_claims.notes: Keeps the acute clinical signal appropriately constrained.

author_claims.claim_text: Collagen scaffold plus hUC-MSC repair shows a continuous preclinical-to-clinical signal across rat, canine, and acute complete human contexts, including control-separated clinical neurological gains, but remains a bundled multi-component strategy.
author_claims.notes: Strong translational path, weaker as isolated scaffold or cell efficacy proof.

author_claims.claim_text: Biomimetic 3D-printed PEGDA-GelMA scaffolds can impose lesion-scale architecture that supports host-graft axonal relay formation and functional recovery when loaded with NPCs; empty scaffolds support host axon entry but not distal host-axon extension or MEP recovery.
author_claims.notes: NPC and scaffold contributions are separated by empty-scaffold, NPC-only, and retransection controls.

author_claims.claim_text: Multi-channel scaffold architecture is a reusable experimental platform for separating geometry, cell, and molecule effects.
author_claims.notes: Platform claim rather than outcome claim.

author_claims.claim_text: Injectable scaffolds can be given tunable alignment after delivery, expanding guidance strategies beyond prefabricated implants.
author_claims.notes: Based on magnetic peptide hydrogel design.

author_claims.claim_text: Microchannel GelMA scaffolds can pair geometry with hAEC-derived neural-like cell placement to support partial repair after complete transection, with 8-week BBB 5.667 versus 2.333 for empty scaffold and 0.667 for transection control and MEP 29.57% of normal.
author_claims.notes: Architecture and cell effects remain bundled; BBB analyses were small and mortality-limited, and cells were not shown to be mature neurons.

author_claims.claim_text: Chronic rat scar resection plus collagen/hUC-MSC scaffold repair improves enough outcome domains to justify chronic scaffold/cell testing.
author_claims.notes: Full-text unavailable, so claim is cautious.

author_claims.claim_text: dECM scaffold plus hNS/PC transplantation can improve chronic lesion histology even when functional recovery remains absent.
author_claims.notes: Useful histology-function boundary in chronic complete SCI.

author_claims.claim_text: Chitosan bridges with immobilized factors are best interpreted as combined scaffold-cell-cue systems rather than scaffold-only interventions.
author_claims.notes: Directly designed as combination therapy.

author_claims.claim_text: Spinal cord-derived dECM/GelMA scaffolds are used to recreate a lesion-local matrix niche for stem-cell survival and repair.
author_claims.notes: Matrix-niche claim; effect attribution remains bundled.

author_claims.claim_text: Collagen scaffold tethering can convert exosome delivery from diffuse bolus logic into a local sustained-release strategy.
author_claims.notes: Based on collagen-binding exosome design.

author_claims.claim_text: Delayed bFGF/HEMA-MOETACL implantation can reduce cavitation, support axon and vessel ingrowth, and improve SSEP/MEP recovery after complete transection, while hydrogel-only effects show that material and trophic contributions are partly separable but not fully independent.
author_claims.notes: Combined group had the strongest axon, vessel, and electrophysiology outcomes; hydrogel alone reduced cavitation without clear behavioral recovery.

author_claims.claim_text: Drug-loaded nanofiber scaffolds can combine physical support with anti-inflammatory treatment after SCI.
author_claims.notes: Methylprednisolone/PCL/PSA anchor.

author_claims.claim_text: Layer-by-layer PEG/PAA/protein films over agarose can provide active, pH-triggered protein release for more than four weeks in vitro, supporting a non-cell-based trophic-delivery method for future channel bridges but not proving SCI efficacy.
author_claims.notes: Lysozyme model protein; BDNF was proposed for subsequent scaffold testing.

author_claims.claim_text: HA hydrogel permissiveness is conditional on astrocyte-ECM identity: protoplasmic ECM reduced GFAP, ED1, and CSPG burden and increased Tuj1 penetration, whereas fibrous ECM did not reproduce the benefit and could negate HA-associated CSPG reduction; V2a aggregates increased neuronal-process staining but were not tested for functional integration.
author_claims.notes: No locomotor endpoint; this is a histology and cell-persistence study.

author_claims.claim_text: Decellularized matrix components in multimodal hydrogels are usually one part of a larger regenerative cocktail.
author_claims.notes: Avoids assigning all benefit to DBM alone.

author_claims.claim_text: Chronic human scar-resection scaffold strategies depend on correctly distinguishing scar-rich target tissue from functionally important spared cord.
author_claims.notes: Cross-module alignment with Module 1B.

author_claims.claim_text: Chronic scar removal plus anisotropic scaffold channels can turn a chronic transection cavity into a guided repair substrate in rodents.
author_claims.notes: Strong chronic animal model claim.

author_claims.claim_text: Composite hydrogels can intentionally combine structural guidance with biochemical regulation, blurring scaffold and cargo categories.
author_claims.notes: AFG/fSAP anchor.

author_claims.claim_text: Surface-capping scaffolds are a distinct repair geometry from implanted lesion bridges and can preserve early neuronal fibers while reducing scar/fibrotic signals in a bundled HA/PPY/PM-CURC-iNPC strategy.
author_claims.notes: HA demilune cap; one-week n=3 study did not reduce Iba1/ED1 inflammation or establish function.

author_claims.claim_text: The scaffold literature should be synthesized by material, cargo, cell source, injury model, chronicity, and outcome class rather than by a single global pro-repair claim.
author_claims.notes: Central synthesis caution.

author_claims.claim_text: Chronic translation requires anatomical compatibility between scaffold strategy and lesion architecture, not just a positive acute rodent repair signal.
author_claims.notes: Cross-module synthesis statement.

boundary_records.boundary_statement: Human scaffold studies in Module 2A support safety/feasibility more than definitive efficacy.
Scaffold-plus-cell studies often cannot separate material effects from cell-source effects.
boundary_records.supporting_evidence: M2B-O004, O009, O011, O032-O036; review anchors M2A-R005-R007

boundary_records.boundary_statement: Histological regeneration signals do not guarantee functional recovery.
ECM-derived materials are not interchangeable; source tissue and immune response can change outcomes.
Chronic scar-resection scaffold strategies assume a lesion geometry where scar/cavity can be targeted without sacrificing spared functional tissue.
boundary_records.supporting_evidence: M2B-O001, O002, O017, O018, O046, O047; Module 1B human lesion architecture

boundary_records.boundary_statement: Functional improvement after scaffold treatment may arise from mechanisms other than axons traversing the scaffold.
Architecture/guidance observations are strongest when scaffold-only or simple controls exist; printed/cell-loaded systems often bundle geometry with graft biology.
Conductive and surface-patch scaffolds are emerging categories and should not be collapsed into passive cavity-filling scaffold claims.

consensus_drafts.draft_statement: Scaffold architecture is best treated as a lesion-topology intervention: aligned fibers, channels, pores, conduits, and printed geometry can organize axon, cell, and tissue growth, but the relevant claim depends on matching the scaffold format to lesion shape, gap size, and endpoint.
consensus_drafts.notes: Supported by O004-O008 and O024-O029; partly confounded by cells/cargo

consensus_drafts.draft_statement: Natural ECM, decellularized matrix, and hydrogel scaffolds provide tissue-like repair environments, but their effects are conditional on ECM source, stiffness/degradation, immune response, vascular integration, lesion model, and whether added cells or factors are present.

consensus_drafts.draft_statement: Chronic scar or cavity scaffold repair is a reconstruction strategy only when lesion anatomy permits safe resection, boundary identification, and gap filling; these rows should be interpreted through Module 1 lesion architecture rather than as generic scaffold efficacy.
